deploybot: [ROLLBACK STARTED] Canary flagged for release-tag v3.2.1 in prod-usw at 2025-11-04T03:12:05Z. Observed spike in runtime-api 5xx and request latency. Initiating automatic rollback to v3.1.9. Rollback ID: rb-0x9f3a. ETA ~6m. Commit/tag info: v3.2.1 -> 9d4c2b, stable v3.1.9 -> 6a1b7f.

olivia: copying logs to thread. Can we confirm there were no DB migrations in v3.2.1? Need to ensure revert doesn't touch schema.

sanjay: quick check: commits in v3.2.1 are app code + routing tweak, no migrations. I grep'd the deploy diff: no migrations/ddl. Safe to roll back from schema perspective.

release-eng: pinging infra to watch for cache invalidation. Also please pin traffic back to v3.1.9 after revert and create a short release note blurb.

mara: oncall:alert set. I've muted noisy alarms and added a post-id trace to correlate. Watching error-rate dashboards.

deploybot: Executing revert command: ```bash
redwoodctl deploy revert --env=prod-usw --from-tag=v3.2.1 --to-tag=v3.1.9 --id=rb-0x9f3a
```

deploybot: [IN-PROGRESS] Reverting services: runtime-api, kv-cache, router. Rolling traffic back via loadbalancer rules. Progress: runtime-api 100% -> running v3.1.9, kv-cache 90% -> draining, router 60%.

olivia: noted. I'll watch the DB connections and heatmap for any anomalies. If we see schema mismatch, we stop and escalate.

oncall-bot: metric alert suppressed: runtime-api 5xxs reduced from 4.2% -> 0.6% (observed in last 90s). ETA adjusted.

deploybot: [ROLLBACK COMPLETE] Revert finished at 2025-11-04T03:16:28Z. Duration 4m23s. Traffic restored to v3.1.9 on prod-usw. Rollback ID rb-0x9f3a. Deployed commits: 6a1b7f pinned. No migrations detected.

release-eng: thanks. I'll draft the changelog: "v3.2.1 reverted due to increased 5xxs and latency on runtime-api; rolled back to v3.1.9 while we investigate." Will open a postmortem ticket and attach repro steps.

mara: verifying downstream: event-processor lag normal, ingestion within SLO. Marking incident as mitigated.

olivia: follow-up actions: 1) Collect kernel/runtime traces from canary hosts, 2) run the failing load test locally against v3.2.1, 3) create a hotfix branch if root cause points to the routing tweak. Assigning to sanjay + infra.

sanjay: ACK. I'll take the traces and start a bisect run. Will post progress in this thread.

deploybot: Note: version pinned to v3.1.9 until release-eng issues a safe-roll-forward. If a re-deploy is attempted, it will require manual approval and a new change window.

release-eng: copying this to #incidents and adding to the weekend change window notes. Thanks team. :thumbsup:
